title: Prove the optimal full-coefficient connector overhead exponent in every finite characteristic (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

For every fixed finite characteristic c >= 3, the unsigned dirty connector with all c^n - 1 nonzero coefficient rows has

```text
OPT_c(n) = c(c^n - 1) + Theta(c^(n/c)).

split n sources into c balanced blocks
for each nonempty block
  run a restored positive-step Hamilton cycle on its coefficient torus
for each output row
  read once at each of its c block projections
```

Claim type: **scoped proof with a deterministic construction and finite corroboration**. This proves the optimal overhead exponent, allowing arbitrary extra readouts in the lower bound. It gives no optimal leading constant, new exact optimum, new kappa or selected-frontier change. Only `research/full-coefficient-connector/` is added.

For n = ac + r >= c, 0 <= r < c, the construction uses S_c(n) = (c + (c - 1)r)c^a source calls and exactly c reads per output. A source path of length L has at most P_c(L) = binomial(L+c-1,c)-L nonzero c-read sums. Extra rows require at least 2c reads. The relaxed invoice is bounded below by c(c^n-1)+L_0, where L_0 is the first c-multiple at least cn with P_c(L_0) >= c^n-1. This is at least c(c^n-1)+(c!(c^n-1))^(1/c)-(c-1).

For full ternary demand, explicit seven- and eight-source words use 6603 and 19743 calls. This continues #4244's larger-source open question. The uniform construction is not best at five or six sources; their cited exact optima remain smaller.

## Evidence

Before: #4238/#4244 give exact full-ternary results at five/six sources and leave larger sizes open. After: a self-contained all-n construction and matching-order lower bound work in every finite characteristic, including composite characteristics.

The verifier checks 41 literal words, 36996 output rows and 186532 calls through formal noncommuting coefficient ledgers; 28 Hamilton cycles; all 780 small weak block compositions; all 2220 multisets in four cases; 12 independent dense executions with dirty registers and singular noncommuting matrices over Z/3, Z/4 and Z/6; and six rejected word/characteristic controls. Its generated stdout receipt binds the counts and examples to all five package file hashes.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/full-coefficient-connector/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/full-coefficient-connector/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/full-coefficient-connector
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/full-coefficient-connector --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 interpreter may replace the local path. Marker: `PASS_FULL_COEFFICIENT_CONNECTOR`. All four commands pass locally. The registered normal/optimized checks took 0.208/0.213 seconds individually; the package runner took 0.738 seconds. The final committed-byte/source-history preflight checks five files and the base ancestor. The card's positive control also passed with `pairings=945 max_coverage=31 queries=74 leaves=182`. These timings establish replay bounds, not performance improvements.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- The all-n claim is the written induction and counting proof. Finite execution is corroboration; there is no proof-kernel certificate or independent human review.
- No global leading constant or exact optimum for n >= 7 is established. The block cost is optimal only within the stated separately restored block geometry.
- Unit complete-call counts only. A consumer needing every coefficient row, coefficient preparation, dispatch, stock, hosting, precision, tape and complete supplier admission are unknown.
- The cited pending small optima are not rechecked or executable dependencies. Source manifests contain historical provenance at the public base. No pending code is imported.
- The selected cold replay and formal build were not run. No registered local obligation is left for CI alone. The selected frontier is unchanged.

## Open next questions

1. Close the constant gap between the counting lower bound and the c-block construction, starting at c = 3 and n divisible by three. Charge positive-step realization and restoration of any proposed additive basis.
2. Improve the seven-source ternary upper bound 6603 toward #4244's cited lower bound 6588.
3. Pin a real full-coefficient-demand consumer and price its complete physical invoice before extending a supplier.

## Related open work

- #4238, head `191a905d7adba6695b079f744140a73e832787a8`: full ternary five-source predecessor. Its 242 rows and 726 minimum readouts agree numerically with this generator; our uniform upper bound is 747 versus its cited exact 744, so no new small optimum is claimed.
- #4244, head `f436d2911351e5be2842208fe96b0b66442323a4`: full ternary six-source predecessor and larger-source handoff. Its 728 rows and 2184 minimum readouts agree numerically; our uniform upper bound is 2211 versus its cited exact 2208. Its stronger seven-source lower bound 6588 is compatible with our 6603 upper bound.
- #4231, head `8a956cbc80dc55697fd3e214812ce567b5eca48f`: same unsigned ring interface with binary-mask demand. Its necessity argument is predecessor context; the full-demand asymptotic theorem concerns a different output set. No shared optimum is recomputed.
- #4225, head `397025101d23195a5193c7912e6cd384eccdbf1c`: five-source binary F3 optimum 108. Different demand; no overlapping full-ternary optimum.
- #4232, head `86ad339efc9f817846479431d8cc0f04edf95fb9`: binary F3 floor/deletion results for every source count. Different demand; no overlapping full-demand number.
- #4250, head `aa61e1746f8c12807bed59cd169591bd82320bc6`: seven-source binary F3 optimum 405. It does not address the 2186-row full ternary demand; no shared optimum.
- #4248, head `e7df122403cfc2febfb6799abb821487d8d1ee49`: binary-mask depth blocks across characteristics. Full coefficient torus blocks are a different construction and demand; no shared optimum.
- #4255, head `0dba831b7e138c809f1900ecf51b4716ea99c505`: parity bounds for the binary-mask floor in even characteristic. It does not settle this full-demand overhead; no overlapping numerical claim.
- #4189, head `5fb3936dfc8082f438f21c72dd6ca49ff4366ae7`: one-source, one-output F3 predecessor. Full one-source demand has two outputs, so its six-call optimum and our nine-call word are different quantities.
- #4236, head `bd9b426837cddd37338dd284e49cc2303de57ca0`: counts optimal words for one nonzero coefficient row. This package serves all rows simultaneously; no shared word-count quantity.

Live overlap covered the recent 100 open PRs, earlier account PRs, all connector-title PR bodies, current handoffs, active Discussion summaries, main-tree formula/object searches and merged searches for full coefficients, ternary demand, characteristic and overhead. The overlap helper reported 364 open PRs and 3129 Discussion records with complete pagination. Arbitrary diffs, unpublished work and literature priority are not exhaustively covered.

## CI notes

Hosted CI is green on head `6a95ef419f94e7b5c2fff710e34081520cc6aba2` in [run 39504635104](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39504635104): `plan` passed in 2m52s and the package `replay` in 1m20s. Both hosted scientific modes printed the same counts and all five file hashes as the local committed replay. The `Committed inputs remain unchanged` step passed. All registered checks, byte/source-history checks and whitespace checks also pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64. No job failed, no rerun was needed, and no registered local obligation was left to CI.

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Blast radius: isolated. Five new package files and their opt-in replay; no shared code or selected source changes.

Correction to the CLAIM: #2208 is by conorholds, not Richardson; Richardson is credited for its #943/#934 lineage. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Apache-2.0.
